1.tell: Informal-sanction option beats formal-machinery options. A market-norms passage that bothers to describe a 'principal item' custom is describing an unwritten code, so the punishment is withdrawal of everyday mutual aid (change, watching, shared ice) rather than a committee levy (D, over-specified: Wednesday, afternoon, back of the shoe shop) or expulsion (C, absolute). B narrows to succession rights, an unrelated mechanism. A is also the only option whose content is a continuous, ongoing sanction, which matches 'is punished when'.

2.tell: Paired-passage 'how would B respond to A's evidence' almost always keys to 'reinterprets the datum inside B's own framework' rather than denial or concession. B is the mineral-glow side (signalled by the manganese/crystal vocabulary appearing in only one option), and D re-explains BOTH halves of A's observation - the going dark and the twenty-minute delay - as store-emptied-then-recharged phosphorescence. A is flat denial (extreme), C concedes the test to A ('behaves the other way round' would refute B), B invents a lamp the stem never mentions.

3.tell: The stem asks why the shift reads as WORSE to Ines, so the key must be about what it reveals of Bell's estimate of her, not about the deck. A supplies exactly that inference (pace judged unfixable, so Bell has dropped to what a slow deckhand can still be taught) and is the longest, most qualified option. D relocates the cause to the deck's condition, which the stem does not ask about; B leaps to an unstated plot (winter run); C contradicts the premise that the correction got smaller.

4.tell: Elimination on the stem's own wording: 'two revivals drawn from THE SAME BOOK' rules out C (different copies) and A (one has punches - that is not drawn from the book), and D explains a difference from the original, not between the two revivals. Only B names a judgment each reviver must make about the same evidence, which is the sole mechanism that produces divergence from identical input - and interpretive-choice options outrank material-circumstance options on 'most strongly suggests' stems.
